summary.headline: Aadhar Housing Q4 FY26: AUM crossed INR30,571 crore (+20% YoY), FY26 PAT INR1,096 crore (+20%), GNPA eased to 1.08%.
summary.overview: Aadhar closed FY26 with AUM of INR30,571 crore, up 20% YoY, and record Q4 disbursements of INR3,087 crore (+20% YoY). FY26 disbursements were INR9,556 crore (+17%) and PAT was INR1,096 crore (+20%), or INR1,108 crore before the one-time Labour Code charge. GNPA was 1.08%, down 30 bps QoQ but up slightly from 1.05% a year earlier, with 1+ DPD improving 78-80 bps QoQ. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 20% AUM growth, about 20% profit growth and 17-18% disbursement growth, with spreads expected to contract 8-10 bps.

financial_highlights.change: -30 bps QoQ; vs 1.05% in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Exit cost of funds / exit spread

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: 73% of AUM; home loan disbursements grew about 26% YoY in Q4, helped by PMAY subsidies (about INR50 crore to about 15,000-16,000 customers) and a push on emerging markets.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP / non-housing)
segments.commentary: 27% of AUM; LAP disbursement mix was about 24-25% in Q4 versus 28-29% typical, deliberately held back since the tariff shock. Management is open to lifting it to 27-28% of disbursements, but not in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Emerging and urban geographies
segments.commentary: Average ticket about INR10.9 lakh on the book. Emerging C is about INR8.5-8.6 lakh, emerging B INR10 lakh, emerging A INR12 lakh, urban INR17-18 lakh. Urban traction is 'encouraging' per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: about 20% AUM growth, about 20% profit growth, and 17-18% disbursement growth.
Spreads expected to contract by about 8-10 bps YoY, given incremental yields of about 13% against a book yield of about 13.52%; partly offset by LAP mix and self-employed shift.
Cost-to-income ratio expected to fall by about 50 bps in FY27, driven by productivity and AI-led sales tools.
Cost of funds expected to hold broadly flat for the next 2-3 quarters; management would be 'very happy' to hold the 7.7% exit rate through FY27.
Direct assignment (DA) volume expected to grow 10-15% in FY27 from about INR1,725 crore in FY26.
Long-term AUM milestone of INR50,000 crore targeted in about 3 years.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 626 across 22 states and more than 550 districts, after 5 branches added in Q4 and 46 in FY26.
Four branch categories: ultra micro (50-60 sq ft), micro, small and main. Small branches take 9-12 months to turn productive and urban branches 12-15 months.
Undrawn sanctions of INR1,687 crore, of which INR246 crore from NHB.
Liquidity of INR1,425 crore at end-Q4 FY26.
Employees: on-roll about 5,400-5,430 and off-roll about 3,900-3,965 at March 2026, versus 4,600 on-roll and 4,300 off-roll a year earlier.
Management expects Uttar Pradesh to be the largest contributor to growth; West Bengal flagged as a potential new state.
demand_pricing: Demand described as end-user driven, with first-time homebuyers prominent. Competition from banks is elevated in urban markets but steady in low-income segments.
Management cited state-level BLC and AHP pipelines (for example, 25,000+ units in Odisha) as supporting demand.
Bounce rates stable for six quarters and unaffected by West Asia conflict; collections team of about 2,000 briefed to be careful.
Low-income segment: management says about 18% share of the low-income HFC peer group, up from 16-17%.
Borrowing mix at March 2026: banks 51%, NHB 22%, NCD 19%, ECB 5%, others 4%. 76% of borrowings are floating; 73-74% of assets are floating.
NCDs are 22% of borrowings, of which 68% are fixed. NHB funding is roughly 50% fixed and 50% floating.

qa_highlights.question: Why has LAP growth lagged, and what is the outlook for other income and ESOP cost?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP slowdown was deliberate since the tariff shock; LAP is 27% of AUM and LAP mix in Q4 was about 26%. Assignment income reflected spreads 80-85 bps better, not larger volumes. About INR6-7 crore of Q4 fee income was one-time. ESOP charge of INR13.5 crore is a Q4 item.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for yields and spreads in FY27 given the rate environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a 2-3 quarter rate hold. Spread contraction of 8-10 bps is guided at the current 25-26% LAP mix. Each 5 percentage points shifted from HL to LAP adds about 400 bps on that portion.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 1+ DPD improvement and the sequential jump in disbursements?
qa_highlights.answer: 1+ DPD fell about 80 bps (not risen, as the analyst framed it) over 18 months of focus on collections. Sequential disbursement strength came from Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Delhi, Karnataka and Uttarakhand. Incremental borrowing cost rose about 10 bps QoQ because bank drawdowns were deferred into Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why did opex-to-AUM rise sequentially in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 always carries sales contests and one-time incentive costs. Cost-to-income improved YoY from 37.9% to 37.1% in Q4. Full-year cost-to-income was 35.9%, down from 36.4%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ticket size trends and the sources of the home loan growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental ticket size ranged INR12.5-13.5 lakh over recent quarters, against INR10.9 lakh on book. Management aims to hold book ticket size at INR10-11.5 lakh, and to hold non-home loans to about 70:30 with home loans over the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the funding book can still reprice, and how far has cost of funds fallen?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental cost fell from 8.4% to 7.6% YoY, with banks passing on 70-75 bps. Exit cost of funds moved from 8.14% to 7.72%, with 15 bps passed to customers. NCDs (22%) are mostly fixed, so the remaining repricing is limited to bank and floating NHB funds.

risks_watch: Geopolitical (West Asia) stress on borrowers; bounce rates and collections are the early indicators to watch.
Spread compression of 8-10 bps YoY if LAP mix stays at about 25-26%; cost of funds could rise given the 76% floating-rate liability book.
Competitive pressure from banks in urban markets.
Ticket size drift: management targets INR10-11.5 lakh, with construction-cost inflation expected to push it higher.
LAP usage is a lever to protect yields but is deferred; delinquency on LAP is about 0.7-0.75% higher on GNPA and must be watched when mix is raised.
Labour Code exceptional charge of INR16 crore taken in Q3; ESOP cost of INR13.5 crore in Q4 is a one-time item per management.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and execution, with guidance reiterated. Cautious and deliberate on LAP and rates, explicitly holding back on LAP and expecting a 2-3 quarter rate hold. Some answers were loose on numbers, with corrections made live (for example, 1+ DPD fell rather than rose).
key_quotes: On all the 3 critical parameters, we have stood by our guidance and commitment to the market.
We don't want to do something in haste, which will go out and look at our delinquency numbers.
Our view is that the interest rate cycle has stagnated and to a certain extent, will be stagnant for at least two, three quarters.

adds.what: Branch network additions: 5 branches added in Q4 FY26 and 46 in FY26 (network at 626 branches); no forward branch count given

growth.why: FY27 guidance held at about 20% AUM growth, about 20% profit growth and 17-18% disbursement growth; backing is partial, with undrawn sanctions of INR1,687 crore, a branch network of 626 with 5 added in Q4 and 46 in FY26, and state BLC/AHP pipelines, but no specific capacity or timed order targets.
